# Reviewer application

**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software that lets a merchant sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and lets the buyer receive the complete result in its existing application.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from award acceptance**. The outcome is two independently operated merchant services, each used by an independent buyer, with two independent buyer operators and the same useful service operating through two independently operated facilitators. The work progresses from installed services by day 30 to recurring testnet use by day 90 and maintainable mainnet operation by day 150.

A purchase connects four records: the buyer’s approved request, the settled transfer, the complete usable output and the merchant’s fulfillment or accounting. The application keeps that connection through interrupted delivery, a changed source edition and transfer to another maintainer.

The existing product is the starting point. The award funds reusable Stellar integration, source and receiving adaptations, deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the selected independent services. Those improvements return to the public product.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API/data-service operator or the agency implementing that service in its customer’s application. The commissioning payer buys the installation and maintainable handover; the independent buyer pays for the useful resource. These roles can belong to different organizations.

An analyst needs the complete selected population, source period, units and usable report. An agent application needs the result it approved and control over aggregate spending. A prepaid customer’s saved call must keep its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change. The merchant needs to connect payment, complete output, its offer and later service or accounting obligations.

Public implementation reports illustrate the gap: a merchant’s payment-bearing calls failed across a GET/POST mismatch; another reported successful settlement with missing Bazaar indexing. These Base reports supply cross-ecosystem implementation learning for our Stellar request, discovery and receiving integration. [Method report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3657) · [Discovery report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3677).

Our own conversations establish commissioning decisions:

|Organization|Observed response and proposed work|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Veridex|Invited an open testnet design partnership after declining a third-party testing budget. The proposed route/buyer adaptation is $1,500 over five business days; payer agreement remains open.|
|CoCart|Its founder asked who introduces and pays for the customer work, how referral compensation works and who contracts. The proposed $7,200 / 60-hour / fifteen-business-day workshare covers one customer’s headless cart, checkout, payment/order operation and receiving.|
|Blockscout|Expressed interest on October 12 and reported no integration budget. The proposed API/buyer installation is $4,800 over ten business days.|
|Nansen|Declined pursuing the proposal on October 12 after an internal referral. Its earlier $2,400 / five-business-day offer remains commissioning history and customer learning.|


The two funded installations and agreements remain to be selected. A resource platform can participate while its merchant, agency or end customer commissions the integration. Bryce owns these relationships and agreements.

Distribution combines direct commissioning by operators with recurring tasks and implementation partnerships with their platforms or agencies. Each workorder names the payer, merchant, buyer, receiving engineer, authorized source, exact operation, full output, priced unit, aggregate task budget, host and acceptance owner. A later period, source edition or distinct query creates the reason to return.

The separate ARS proposal applies this approach to one environmental client-network source/reporting installation: $6,400 over fifteen business days, with $3,200 at kickoff and $3,200 at accepted delivery. Its existing source/reporting product provides an operating foundation.

TokenJunkieLabs sells defined implementation and separately scoped care; merchants retain their resource receipts. Delivery effort, corrections, support time and collections inform later pricing. Customer benefit is less active effort and fewer manual corrections from approved purchase to useful output, with a service another engineer can operate.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies the settlement for the operation the buyer approved. Each approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator verify and settle that authorization. The application associates the returned settlement with the original request, complete output and merchant action. The buyer retains signing and aggregate spending authority; the merchant controls its resource and terms.

We compose the existing x402 Exact Stellar scheme, SDKs, token contracts and facilitators, including the selected provider’s actual payment requirements and optional discovery extension. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery model.

There are close alternatives. [ApiCharge](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements. [Nirium](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides Stellar payment SDKs, seller middleware, MCP and CLI interfaces. [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) supplies service discovery and paid calls; [Stellar Raven](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) supplies ecosystem context and integration operations through MCP. Our application completes the customer’s continuing operation around payment: source review, complete paginated or file output, receiving into its business application, interrupted-operation recovery, and transfer of the working service to another maintainer.

We propose [Open Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track) for this reusable merchant-and-buyer operating application. The funded contribution is the source-to-result and receiving workflow across independent services, with published implementation and deployment improvements. The same-service, two-facilitator deliverable includes the required registration and payment-policy integration. The retained catalogue comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity, so this package includes real same-service registration and compatibility. Repeat independent purchases and successfully operated customer installations measure the value to Stellar.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The architecture has six components: a private merchant source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the Stellar SDK and facilitator; private buyer approval and spending state; retained delivery records and complete output; and merchant fulfillment/accounting.

1. **Select and publish.** The merchant chooses an authorized source edition or named live query, schema, output and limits. Review resolves the route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **Connect the source.** Adapters preserve types, null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select access. The returned result identifies its source edition.
3. **Approve and pay.** The buyer retains the HTTP method or MCP tool, arguments, scope and payment option. The remote schema and full challenge, including authorization lifetime, must match before signing. For paid MCP, the endpoint, tool and arguments remain separate from the payment resource; the official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. Per-payment limits and the existing reservation/budget owner govern aggregate spending.
4. **Settle and receive.** The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the network, asset, parties and atomic amount. The application retains the complete output, merchant notification and receiving acknowledgment. A multi-request acquisition keeps its aggregate cost and unfinished coverage. Saved prepaid calls retain their selected pass; a replacement links to its predecessor and acquired results remain available.
5. **Use and account.** The receiving application opens every page and file needed for the task. Merchant pricing connects the selected tariff and saved uniform quote to an actual usage period, counting basis and supplier-cost basis. A reviewed price change carries its measured source into the customer quotation and original invoice or service records.
6. **Recover and hand over.** Server confirmation, observed transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain signed response is reconciled through its original dispatch. The receiving engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the same operation.

Node.js supplies the merchant, buyer, browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their native semantics. The maintained implementation also uses Python and SQLite for typed data and saved queries, and PHP for WordPress/WooCommerce integration. New contracts are outside this six-package request; the product uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

## Working product and demonstrated results

The retained development register contains **18 distinct team-operated purchases totaling 411,000 stroops (0.0411 native testnet XLM)**, with fees recorded separately. Each links its original transaction to complete output. Independent customer usage is the funded next stage.

Representative completed operations demonstrate the common customer workflow:

|Operation|Completed outcome|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Municipal data|A Queens HPD selection received all 144 rows in paid pages of 100 and 44. Both 10,000-stroop transfers finalized, and the complete CSV/JSONL edition reopened with its source and accounting.|
|Paid agent query|One 50,000-stroop purchase returned 100 MariaDB rows, 14 columns and 53,468 bytes. The purchase reopened with signing disconnected; the complete result reopened in another directory.|
|Filing analysis|A 10,000-stroop purchase delivered the 2024–2025 Genpact comparison: four disclosure pairs, five findings and all 1,027,807 bytes. The editable analyst workspace and a restored installation reopened the same comparison.|
|Air-quality reporting|One public-archive request retained all 140 observations across six sensor series for Del Norte’s May 3, 2022 local day. The reviewed HTML/JSON report reached a separate seven-file customer project and reopened without another source call.|
|Pipeline operations|The OpenLineage service-level workspace completed report export, editable receiving, cold reopening and replay of thirteen original requests. The receiving workspace retained revision 13 and the identical 66-file application export.|


A paid API operation acquired an eight-unit plan for 10,000 stroops and completed a saved four-value analysis. The execution consumed two units; its original request reopened with six available. Ten merchant and eight subsequent agent stages retained the order, full result, allowance and settlement outbox. An encrypted backup continued from 4,096 bytes to all 144,771 bytes after shutdown and reopened offline. A separate local portfolio operation preserved the selected pass across default changes, replacement and archiving, with no extra allowance on replay; its eighteen exercised operations add usage/recovery experience to the network-purchase baseline.

The original merchant accounting exercise completed invoice issue, credit, receipt allocation, Xero-format receiving, correction and cold reopening. The tariff example completed selection, native repricing, backup and receiving: a 1,250-request graduated tariff totaled $14.25 and produced the saved $0.0114 uniform quote.

The installed product also delivers named reports, spreadsheets and supporting files through Jobs and Resource library, retaining the original request, payment and completed attempt. Its Federal awards report preserves the source observations, every transaction page, exact monetary values and editable HTML/JSON/CSV analysis. The OpenLineage Quality extension adds dataset rules, saved evaluations and reasoned findings to the same operating workspace. These are source and receiving foundations for the selected customer adaptations.

The [current merged product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/386) connects recorded usage to a reviewed price and customer quote, and includes the original billing, service agreement, payment plan and customer-closing operators in both merchant installation selections. Its customer continuation has produced the revised quotation and recipient work; the existing operator is continuing the joined interface and financial operation from that saved state.

The complete release also underwent an operator edit, recovered export and separate offline receiving, retaining all 2,411 entries and 2,115 unique objects. The merchant receiving operation completed twelve phases of source/result reads, interruption recovery, file delivery and cold receiving with zero additional payments.

A captioned 3-minute-32-second product/team film follows a native query, saved terms, one 0.005-testnet-XLM purchase, complete result, download and reopening. The source and operating documentation are maintained together with the public product.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are included in the 50-hour/$4,750 response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network, facilitator, protected records, observation sources, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

It covers changed offers or approvals, incorrect payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted delivery, lost observation and restoration of the wrong generation. The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Both retain notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery states, response/recovery times, corrections and the receiving engineer’s reopening after restart. Monitoring gaps remain visible until observation resumes.

|Measure|Counting and acceptance|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Completed purchase|One distinct approved intent, independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Deduplicate transactions per network; retain asset amounts and fees separately.|
|Prepaid purchase|Count the settled pass once, with at least one agreed operation and complete accepted output. Further calls and allowance units are usage. An unused pass retains unfinished fulfillment; a replacement needs its own settlement and first useful completion.|
|Complete customer task|Receive and accept every agreed page, file or application result. Retain started tasks, aggregate cost and unfinished coverage beside individual priced requests.|
|Independent and returning buyers|Count the accountable organization/person across its agents and wallets. Both merchants need independent use. Return use requires a distinct qualifying purchase on another UTC day.|
|Two facilitators|Complete the same useful service, schema, source population and output through each independent operator, preserving the actual terms and financial result.|
|Recovery and handover|Continue original requests and financial outcomes; reopen selected files/history, reconcile later operations and complete the maintainer’s support case.|


The seven- and fourteen-day cohorts retain all attempted, completed, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. The purchase window uses original native settlement time, and complete accepted output must be observed by the cutoff. Those timestamps remain separate. The reviewed customer/operator declarations establish independence; team activity retains its own baseline.

For each installation, compare the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on the same source population or period and expected output: active effort, manual corrections, time to useful output, acceptance and unresolved work. Pricing measurements retain quantity, period, counting basis and supplier-cost coverage. Commercial measures use agreed scope, accepted milestones, issued fees, actual collections and support effort from the original workorder/accounting records.

## Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

Bryce is accountable for allocating contributors and operating resources to the six packages. The retained resource study uses 400 hours over 150 days. Its lowest examined timely allocation is 25 engineering hours plus eight integration/handover hours per week. This is a modeled allocation; named contributor availability and payment arrangements are being finalized against the actual award date.

SCF’s four payments would be **$3,800 at award acceptance, then $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective deliverables are approved**. These payment amounts differ from tranche delivery costs. The USD-equivalent award is paid in XLM; the applicable settlement price is the value reported on the actual payment day, under the [Official Rules](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/official-rules-for-submissions).

Grant and accepted commercial work share one contributor capacity plan. A commissioned workshare adds its actual hours, dependencies and acceptance dates; available hours are allocated once. Bryce reconciles the combined schedule and expected collections before agreeing dated work, using separately named capacity or agreed timing changes.

The resource model makes the working-capital requirement explicit. With its labor-accrual assumptions, additional peak cash is $17,250 at a 14-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days. Opening cash and a committed bridge or contributor deferral have not been entered. Actual available funds, client collections and agreed contributor payment timing must cover the modeled requirement before the corresponding delivery commitments are made.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of the preceding payment. For an anticipated delay, we will obtain SDF’s written acknowledgment before the original deadline and use a revised deadline only when confirmed in writing.

Sustainability comes from reusable open-source deployment and receiving capabilities, paid customer-specific implementation and separately scoped care. Workorders retain delivery effort, included corrections, support responsibilities, acceptance and collections. Reusable work completed before award is removed from the remaining estimate, keeping the grant focused on the agreed prospective Stellar development.
